etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English famous, from Anglo-Norman famous, from Latin fāmōsus, equivalent to fame +‎ -ous. Displaced native Old English hlīsful.

quote.citation: c. 1587–1588, [Christopher Marlowe], Tamburlaine the Great.  […]  The First Part […], 2nd edition, part 1, London:  […]  [R. Robinson for] Richard Iones, […], published 1592, →OCLC; reprinted as Tamburlaine the Great (A Scolar Press Facsimile), Menston, Yorkshire, London: Scolar Press, 1973, →ISBN, Act III, scene iii:
quote.text: By this my ſword that conquer’d Perſea,Thy fall ſhall make me famous through the world:

definitions.definition: (transitive, obsolete) To make famous; to bring renown to.
